source.title: GraphGPT: Generative Pre-trained Graph Eulerian Transformer
source.authors: Qifang Zhao; Weidong Ren; Tianyu Li; Hong Liu; Xing-Sheng He; Xiaoxiao Xu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The scaling results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports graph-model pretraining-loss scaling plots, extending loss-scaling measurements to graph data rather than language-model text pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as motivation but does not test their language-model claims. It reports log-log plots of graph pretraining and fine-tuning losses against model size, and graph pretraining loss against training tokens. No fitted exponents, quantitative extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocation results are stated.
record.test_reason: The study trains graph transformers (GraphGPT) from 4.2M to 2B non-embedding parameters. It plots self-supervised pretraining loss and fine-tuning loss against parameter count on log-log axes (Fig. 3) and pretraining loss against tokens (Figs. 4–5). This is a new modality bearing on V5. However, no power law is fitted and no point values are stated in the text.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right. The authors also claim consistent performance gains when scaling to 2B parameters, framed in Q10 as following Kaplan/Hoffmann to catalyse graph scaling-law work. They also note diminishing returns from adding external molecular pretraining data on PCQM4Mv2. No fitted law is given.
record.recipe_differences: This is a graph-learning model study. It measures graph pretraining and fine-tuning losses over selected model sizes and token counts, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy or fixed-compute allocations; it reports no fitted exponents.
record.method_sensitivity: The ogbl-citation2 token-loss plots vary edge-ego subgraph sampling (d=1, n=14 or n=30).

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream graph-task metrics improve with model size, with a plateau at the top of the PCQM4Mv2 range. PCQM4Mv2 valid MAE goes 0.0827/0.0807/0.0793/0.0792 (M/B12/B24/B48). ogbl-ppa HR@100 goes 65.44/68.76/76.55 (M/B/XXL). ogbn-proteins ROC-AUC goes 83.56/84.02/85.33 (S/M/B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream performance of graph transformers improves monotonically with parameter count (graph-modality analogue of V6).

fits_no_version.finding: Table 7: node re-indexing raises pretraining loss (0.0844→0.0874 at 4.48M; 0.0689→0.0750 at 114M) yet improves downstream AP. Lower pretraining loss therefore does not track downstream performance across this data-augmentation choice.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining loss is not a reliable predictor of downstream performance when data augmentation changes (graph analogue of V6).

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; the text identifies the Proceedings of the 41st ICML, PMLR 267 (2025).
record.problems: For the scaling plots, the text supplies no exact loss values, uncertainty estimates, fitted exponents, or fit diagnostics; the plotted curves alone do not establish power-law behavior.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or exponent for graph pretraining loss. No data-size scaling with separately trained runs. No image, video or repeated-data regimes.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
Shape variation exists (B24 vs B48 vs L) but is not analysed at fixed parameter count.

missing.what: Pretraining loss by model size on ogbg-molpcba: 0.0844 (4.48M) vs 0.0689 (114.12M) without re-indexing, and 0.0874 vs 0.0750 with re-indexing. These are the only numeric loss-vs-size values in the paper.
Downstream metric by model size across PCQM4Mv2, molpcba, ogbl-ppa, ogbl-citation2, ogbn-proteins and ogbn-arxiv.

record.verdict_notes: No labels are given. Every row linked to V5 is figure-only, and the text gives no fitted law. The only numeric loss-vs-size evidence (Table 7) covers two sizes, which shows lower loss with size but cannot establish a power-law form. The token figures are single-run learning curves under linear-decay schedules, not data-scaling sweeps. Graph data is treated as a new modality under V5.

versions.untested_parts: The models and losses are for graph learning, not held-out language-model pretraining loss.
No prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs is reported.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is reported.
The study does not compare architecture details such as depth and width at fixed parameter count for their effect on loss.
The study tests graph-model loss scaling, but not image or video models, repeated-data effects, or power-law behavior in transfer or fine-tuning beyond the displayed graph-task fine-tuning-loss plot.
The study reports downstream task results but does not test whether downstream performance is predictably related to pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
No comparison of fitting choices, fitted exponents, or systematic curve bending is reported.
